messages:
tina: Quick heads-up — Zenith demo POC hitting repeated SSE disconnects in Safari during long responses. Customer shows UI stalling and partial JSON objects. They also attached the security questionnaire and asked about Dedicated pricing — blocking the deal. Need triage and a short script to repro for them. :eyes:

emma: ugh, Safari has weird stream buffering. Is the client using native EventSource or a fetch/stream polyfill?

tina: native EventSource in their in-house app. They tried Chrome and it works. Only Safari 15/16.

raj: can we get the exact headers coming from our side? proxies often set `Transfer-Encoding: chunked` but then gzip + buffering at CDN can coalesce chunks.

chris: putting logs here. saw connection closed from client with SSE close code 1006 a few times. server didn't send close. snippet:
```
[2026-03-18T15:12:03Z] conn_id=abc123 keepalive=1 last_event_sent=12
[2026-03-18T15:12:11Z] conn_id=abc123 write_error: broken pipe
[2026-03-18T15:12:11Z] conn_id=abc123 client_ip=1.2.3.4
```

chris: also saw spikes of 502 from our edge while the origin continued streaming — likely proxy reset.

luis: FYI SDK had a bug where multi-byte UTF-8 split across SSE chunks caused the client parser to throw in some Safari builds. PR fixed it but only in v0.9.2+. Are they on an older SDK?

emma: ask them to run a repro curl first: `curl -N -H "Accept: text/event-stream" \"<POC_URL>?session=zenith\"`
If curl sees continuous chunks, then it's likely the browser/CDN. If curl drops too, probably server/edge.

tina: sent curl command to customer. They ran it and said curl holds the connection but stops receiving after ~18s of silence. Their browser shows partial JSON and then parser error.

raj: that matches proxy idle-timeout or keepalive mismatch. What are our SSE heartbeat settings?

chris: default heartbeat is 15s. We send `:heartbeat\n\n` every 15s. But if there are large events and the kernel TCP buffer/psmtp coalesces, Safari might wait for final newline. Also some CDNs buffer until buffer size hits threshold or gzip block completes.

emma: short mitigation: reduce heartbeat to 6-8s and send a small comment line `: \\n` every 5s to force flush. Also ensure `Cache-Control: no-transform` so intermediate proxies don't gzip-chunk.

raj: good call. I'll push a temporary canary config to the POC route: heartbeat=6s + `Cache-Control: no-transform` + `Connection: keep-alive`. Will also add `X-Accel-Buffering: no` for nginx.

chris: deployed canary. infra-bot shows a few 429s earlier from their IP — rate limits hit while they were hammering the stream for debug. logs: `rate_limit: tokens_exhausted, 429`. That could explain abrupt closes when token bucket flushes.

tina: I told them to pause aggressive polling. Can we whitelist their test IP for the POC so they don't hit rate limits while we triage?

raj: done — whitelisted 1.2.3.4 for next 2 hours.

luis: For the SDK: if they can't upgrade, recommend using `event-source-polyfill` for Safari as a temporary client-side workaround. Also the Node/websocket fallback in our SDK can resume streams if the SSE parsing fails — but needs server-side support enabled.

tina: security question: they want SOC2 + logs retention policy and ability to run Dedicated in their VPC. Can someone from infra/enterprise send a short note? This is holding signatures.

chris: I'll draft: we support Dedicated with VPC peering, KMS integration, audit logs (90/365 day tiers). Send details to legal/security and I'll loop in sales engineering for SLA.

emma: quick checklist we gave them to try now:
1) curl -N test (done)
2) reproduce in Chrome vs Safari (done)
3) try `event-source-polyfill` on Safari
4) capture browser console parser error (screenshot)
5) confirm SDK version (upgrade to v0.9.2+ if <0.9.2)
6) test again after we flip heartbeat to 6s

tina: customer will try polyfill + confirm SDK. Also asked about pricing for Dedicated — is there a rough delta vs hosted for POC?

raj: quick answer — Dedicated minimum monthly commit for POC is typically 1 GPU-reserved lane, pricing varies by region. I'll pull numbers and send a short quote.

tina: thanks. If we can get the customer to repro with curl showing continuous small comment heartbeats and Safari still failing, we'll need a packet capture + CDN edge config review.

emma: agree. If patching heartbeat + no-transform fixes it, that's the fastest path. I'll prepare a one-file patch we can flip in the rollout and a small note to their engineering team. :thumbsup:

tina: perfect — I'll update the customer and ask for SDK version + console screenshot. Back to you all once they confirm. Thanks! :raised_hands:
